findings.title: The computable-set oracle in Remark4.4 does not preserve the stated halting obstruction
locations: Printed1924 / PDF4, Definition2.2 and computable-open-set explanation
Printed1930 / PDF10, Remark4.4 and the identity-map exclusion used at the end of Proposition4.3
findings.relation_to_parent_finding: Corroboration and direct Reeb-class extension of the parent's Definition2.2 target-set finding; not an additional independent Major count.
findings.claim_checked: Definition2.2 permits an input-dependent computable open target, described as explicitly approximable to any desired precision. Remark4.4 postulates an oracle deciding intersection of computable sets, but then states that reachability for a Turing-complete system remains undecidable even with this oracle and uses that claim to exclude Seifert flows.
analytic_proof: Fix a universal Turing machine and an initial configuration c. Let t(c)>=1 be its halting time when it halts, and define r_c=2^{-t(c)} in that case, r_c=0 otherwise.

The real r_c is uniformly computable from c: for requested error 2^{-N}, simulate N steps. If halting has occurred, output the exact 2^{-t}; otherwise output0. Any later halting gives r_c<=2^{-(N+1)}, so the error is within the requested bound. Deciding whether this computable real is zero remains the halting problem.

Take the identity discrete dynamical system on the real line, the fixed rational point p_c=0, and the always nonempty bounded interval U_c=(-r_c,1). Its endpoints are uniformly computable; it is uniformly effectively open and its closure has explicit arbitrary-precision interval approximations. The positive orbit {0} intersects U_c exactly when r_c>0, exactly when the machine halts.

Consequently, under the ordinary effective/approximable-open representations admitted by the written explanation, the reachability definition allows the target geometry alone to encode halting. It does not establish the asserted exclusion of the identity map or force complicated dynamics.

The same witness lies directly inside the Reeb/Seifert class. On the standard Sasakian S^3, take the Hopf field R=partial_phi1+partial_phi2 and the fixed point (z1,z2)=(3/5,4/5), whose coordinates are rational and satisfy |z1|^2+|z2|^2=1. The quantity |z1|^2 is invariant along its orbit and equals9/25.

Set U_c={z in S^3: |z1|^2>9/25-r_c}. This is a nonempty open set with uniformly computable threshold and finite-precision descriptions. The Hopf orbit through the fixed point intersects U_c iff9/25>9/25-r_c, iff r_c>0, iff halting. Thus the written weak target-set criterion also labels this simple periodic Seifert flow Turing complete.

For the standard compatible round Sasakian metric, the Hopf field is Killing, so L_R g=0 and the nonnegative Chern-Hamilton energy E(g) is zero. This is a critical minimum in the paper's stated local-minimum sense. The witness does not identify that field with the stronger Corollary4.2 construction.

An oracle deciding intersection of arbitrary computable sets can decide whether {0} intersects (-r_c,1), and therefore decides the original ordinary halting problem. Its power cannot be added while simultaneously asserting that ordinary halting remains undecidable. A relativized universality statement would require a new machine/oracle model, which is not provided in the remark.
counterevidence_considered: The point is exactly rational and independent of the input, so the witness does not exploit an uncomputable initial condition.
The interval target is always nonempty and has computable endpoints, so the issue does not depend on deciding whether an empty effectively open set has been presented.

If 'computable open' were replaced by an explicitly narrower target representation with the required decidability/separation conditions, this particular witness could be excluded. Such restrictions are not stated and should be formulated rather than inferred.

The article's actual constructions encode successive Turing configurations in the orbit, which is substantially stronger than the bare reachability definition. This finding does not refute those cited step-by-step constructions.
The Hopf example refutes the broad exclusion under the weak definition, not the intended Proposition4.3 statement about the specifically constructed Corollary4.2 flow.
findings.impact: Remark4.4's oracle argument is invalid, and its broad exclusion of Seifert/identity dynamics is not supported by Definition2.2 as written. Arguments using such exclusions must fix the target representation or invoke the stronger actual simulation property.
findings.repair: Specify the effective representation and allowed complexity of targets and the uniform encoding, or formulate the stronger configuration-by-configuration simulation actually used in the constructions. Remove the claim that an unrestricted computable-set-intersection oracle preserves undecidability of the original halting problem. Prove the specific critical-metric obstruction geometrically as in CORE-0449-F2.
findings.check_method: Analytic computability and invariant-function calculations; no numerical test or author-code execution was used.

findings.title: Proposition4.3 compares return maps on different transverse disks without justification
findings.claim_checked: After obtaining orbital conjugacy to R_lk=l*partial_phi1+k*partial_phi2, the proof chooses the standard Hopf disk D1={phi1=0}. It then uses identity of the original construction's return map near a different disk boundary to conclude that the standard D1 rotation has angle0 modulo2*pi.
analytic_proof: The printed return angle is correct: on D1, the first return time is2*pi/l and the advance of phi2 is2*pi*k/l. Actual PDF10 was inspected; no inverted-ratio error is asserted.

Return maps on different sections need not be conjugate. For R_{2,1}=2*partial_phi1+partial_phi2, D1={phi1=0} has return time pi and a half-turn in phi2. On D2={phi2=0}, the return time is2*pi and the advance of phi1 is4*pi, so the return map is the identity. Thus the existence of an identity return map on one disk does not force the chosen standard Hopf disk's return angle to vanish.

An orbital conjugacy maps the constructed section to some transverse section. The proof does not show that this image is the particular standard D1 section. The counterexample diagnoses that comparison step; it is not a counterexample to the intended obstruction for the selected universal construction.
repair_proof_conditional_on_cited_classi: Retain the source's imported implications: a critical compatible metric on this S^3 contact structure is Sasakian, and its Reeb flow is orbitally conjugate to a weighted Hopf flow R_lk with l,k>0. These external classification statements were not independently verified in this bounded check.
The constructed return map is the identity on a nonempty annular neighborhood of the disk boundary. Its suspension therefore gives a nonempty open region of periodic flow orbits.

If l/k is irrational, a weighted Hopf flow has no periodic orbit where both complex coordinates are nonzero: closing would require both l*T and k*T to be integer multiples of2*pi. Its only periodic orbits are the two coordinate circles, which have empty interior. Orbital conjugacy preserves periodicity and openness, so the open periodic region excludes irrational l/k.
Therefore l/k must be rational. A common period then closes every weighted Hopf orbit, so every orbit of the constructed flow would be closed.

The actual construction, rather than the weak Definition2.2 alone, gives an injective step-by-step encoding of a universal reversible machine into a disk return map. At least one initial run is nonhalting and never repeats a configuration: otherwise simulating until either halting or a repeated finite configuration would decide every initial halting problem, contradicting universality.

That run produces an aperiodic return orbit under the injective encoding. In the constructed suspension/Poincare realization, a closed flow orbit gives a periodic sequence of returns to the compact transverse section. Hence this encoded orbit cannot be closed.

This contradicts rational weighted Hopf behavior and proves the intended obstruction for the specific Corollary4.2 construction, subject to the cited classification inputs. No computability of the orbital conjugacy and no general assertion that every rotation fails Definition2.2 are required.
counterevidence_and_scope: The noncriticality conclusion is not refuted; the construction has stronger information that supplies a short geometric repair.
The argument is restricted to the selected reversible-universal construction with its periodic collar. It does not cover every Reeb realization allowed by the arbitrary-map statement of Theorem4.1.
Taking the disk map to be the identity in Theorem4.1 can lead to ordinary Hopf/Sasakian examples with critical compatible metrics, so the specific Corollary4.2 choice is essential.
Criticality is interpreted in the stated compatible-metric setting for the fixed contact data; this is not a blanket exclusion of all metrics that make some unrelated field Beltrami.
findings.impact: The printed implication omega=0 modulo2*pi does not follow from the data given. The intended new consequence remains supported by the repaired periodic-orbit argument and the actual step-by-step construction.
findings.repair: Replace the comparison of the two disk return maps by the periodic-region/rational-weights/aperiodic-encoded-orbit argument above, and refer explicitly to the selected Corollary4.2 field.
findings.check_method: Manual exact return-time calculation and analytic orbit argument. No numerical experiment or external classification verification is claimed.

checks.claim: The prime-power encoding and disjoint interval idea work, but two displayed coordinate translations must be corrected.
checks.reasoning: With compactly supported binary tape, the finite strings r=t_b...t_0 and s=t_(-a)...t_(-1) recover the nonnegative and negative tape halves under the stated leading-nonzero/empty convention. Unique factorization makes phi(q,t)=1/(2^q 3^r 5^s) injective. For distinct positive integer denominators A<B, 1/A-1/B >= 1/(A(A+1)); intervals of radius at most (1/4)A^-2 and (1/4)B^-2 are disjoint because their radius sum is <=1/(2A^2)<1/(A(A+1)) for A>=2. Thus the claimed small interval construction is consistent. However, I_(q,t) is a one-dimensional interval, so I_(q,t)^j must be I_(q,t)+2j before taking its Cartesian product with a y-interval; the printed +(2j,2j) has the wrong dimension. Similarly the initial point for the band [2i,2i+1] must be (2i+phi(ci),0), not (i+phi(ci),0). For i=1 the printed point has x in (1,2), outside its assigned band [2,3].
checks.counterevidence: The text immediately defines bands [2j,2j+1], Figure 2 shows those bands, and the curve interpolation formula on p.1933 uses 2i+phi(q_k,t_k). These provide a direct local repair. No refutation of the imported Euclidean construction follows.
checks.repair: Replace I_(q,t)+(2j,2j) by I_(q,t)+2j, and replace p_ci=(phi(ci)+i,0) by p_ci=(phi(ci)+2i,0).

checks.claim: Weak robustness on the unbounded encoding is a fine, decaying-error property, not robustness under a uniform perturbation on a compact state space.
checks.reasoning: The simulated configurations repeat at successively increasing heights k along a curve in the band of a fixed input i. Repetition of a machine configuration therefore does not force geometric recurrence of a planar gradient trajectory. For a gradient field d(f(gamma(t)))/dt=|grad f|^2, so this unbounded coding is compatible with absence of nonconstant periodic gradient orbits. The paper constructs normal contraction toward the coding curves and asks for an error bound epsilon(x,y) that becomes sufficiently small at infinity because the configuration intervals have no uniform positive size. This is a weighted/fine perturbation condition. To pass from f to F one must control first derivatives, e.g. |grad F-grad f| below that error bound; a mere bound on |F-f| would not imply this. Reference [12] is expressly a theorem about a function and its derivatives, consistent with that requirement.
checks.counterevidence: The source repeatedly labels this weak robustness and explicitly explains the shrinking coding sets. It does not claim immunity to arbitrary fixed-amplitude noise or the compact robustness excluded by the cited result in Section 6.
checks.limits: The detailed normal-contraction estimates, choice of the full error function, and full derivative-approximation theorem remain imported from [7] and [12]; they were not independently reconstructed in full. Their omission from an expressly labeled sketch is not promoted into a finding.

checks.claim: The tangent Cauchy datum for curl u=lambda u must be a planar gradient, and the compatible augmented system propagates the missing curl constraint.
checks.reasoning: The principal symbol is i times the cross-product matrix of xi; it annihilates xi and has determinant zero, so ordinary non-characteristic CK cannot be applied directly to arbitrary three-component curl data. If u3(x,y,0)=0, the third curl equation gives partial_x v2-partial_y v1=0. On simply connected R2 this is equivalent to v=grad F; for analytic v the potential can be chosen analytic. For constant real lambda!=0, augment the first two curl equations with div u=0 to obtain partial_z u=A u, where A=[[0,lambda,partial_x],[-lambda,0,partial_y],[-partial_x,-partial_y,0]]. Let H=partial_x u2-partial_y u1-lambda*u3. Substituting this system gives partial_z H=0. For initial data (F_x,F_y,0), H=0 initially and hence everywhere the solution exists. Thus all three curl equations, as well as divergence freeness, hold.
checks.limits: The sign convention was checked against the actual displayed curl equations. This verifies the compatibility mechanism without claiming the article directly applies ordinary CK to the singular curl system.

checks.claim: Theorem 5.2's entire hypothesis supplies a global spatial extension; it is stronger than mere real analyticity.
checks.reasoning: Let a=(F_x,F_y,0) be entire on C2 and define u(x,y,z)=sum_(k>=0) z^k A^k a(x,y)/k! with A from L04. To justify convergence, introduce G(x,y,w)=exp(lambda*w)a(x,y) and replace every multiplication by lambda in A by partial_w, obtaining a first-order constant-coefficient matrix operator B. Every component of B^k G is a sum of at most 2^k derivatives of total order k. On a complex polydisc of radius R around a fixed compact set, Cauchy's estimate bounds each such derivative by k! M_R/R^k. Therefore |A^k a| <= 2^k k! M_R/R^k. For any compact |z|<=Z choose R>2Z; the defining series converges locally uniformly by a geometric majorant and defines an entire function on C3. It solves partial_z u=A u termwise, has the prescribed data, and L04 gives curl u=lambda u. If F is real on R2 and lambda real, the resulting field is real on R3. For uniqueness among smooth Beltrami fields, lambda!=0 implies div u=0 and Delta u+lambda^2 u=0. Elliptic analyticity and the determined normal derivatives give local uniqueness, continued over connected R3.
checks.counterevidence: The actual theorem explicitly defines 'entire' as holomorphic extension to C2. It does not infer global existence merely from ordinary real-analytic local CK.
checks.limits: This verifies global spatial definition of the vector field. It is not a separate proof that every trajectory from every initial point is complete for all real time. Detailed global-time behavior of the imported coding construction was not independently re-established.

checks.claim: A compatible Beltrami extension transfers the planar step-by-step simulation through an invariant plane.
checks.reasoning: The Cauchy datum has third component zero on z=0, so that plane is invariant by uniqueness of the smooth ODE. The restricted field is exactly grad F. Lift each actual planar coded input p to (p,0); for a planar halting target U take U times (-eta,eta), with any fixed eta>0. A trajectory starting on the plane enters that open three-dimensional target exactly when its planar trajectory enters U. This uses the actual configuration-by-configuration construction described in Sections 2.2 and 5.2, rather than deriving physical simulation solely from the weak abstract wording of Definition 2.2.
checks.limits: The parent owns separate issues concerning Definition 2.2's effective quantifiers and target representation. Those findings are not duplicated or dismissed here; this transfer concerns the stronger actual simulator.

checks.claim: The Euclidean constant-eigenvalue Beltrami construction has the stated infinite-energy limitation.
checks.reasoning: For a nonzero smooth field satisfying curl u=lambda*u with constant real lambda!=0, divergence freeness and curl-curl imply Delta u+lambda^2 u=0. If u were in L2(R3), its L2 Fourier transform would be supported on the sphere |xi|^2=lambda^2 (up to Fourier normalization). That sphere has Lebesgue measure zero, so the transform and u would vanish. Thus the nontrivial field used for the actual simulator cannot have finite kinetic energy. The introduction explicitly acknowledges infinite energy.
checks.limits: This argument is specific to nonzero constant-lambda Beltrami fields on Euclidean R3. It does not prove that every finite-energy steady Euler flow is incapable of computation, nor does it apply to compact manifolds with an adapted metric.

checks.claim: Under Remark 6.1's Hodge-Laplacian viscosity and the unrestricted metric in Open problem 4, a suspension of the article's actual area-preserving simulator already gives an affirmative example.
proof: Input simulator: use the area-preserving disk diffeomorphism phi supplied by Proposition 4.1 from a reversible universal generalized shift. It is the identity near the boundary and carries the actual step-by-step computation on its encoded Cantor set. Extend phi by the identity to a closed oriented surface Sigma=S2, choosing an area form omega that equals the preserved disk area form there. The extension remains smooth and omega-preserving.

Closed manifold and flow: form the mapping torus M=(Sigma x [0,1])/((x,1)~(phi(x),0)). The vector field X=partial_t, the one-form alpha=dt, and the volume form mu=dt wedge omega descend. M is a smooth closed compact three-manifold. The return map from t=0 to t=0 is phi. X is smooth, nowhere zero, and complete by compactness.

Smooth metric with controlled seam: choose any surface metric h0 with area form omega. Let beta:[0,1]->[0,1] be smooth, equal to 0 near 0 and equal to 1 near 1. Put k_t=(1-beta(t))*h0+beta(t)*phi^*h0. These are positive definite metrics; write vol(k_t)=f_t*omega with f_t>0. In dimension two, define h_t=k_t/f_t, so vol(h_t)=omega. At the endpoints f_0=f_1=1 because phi preserves omega, hence h_1=phi^*h_0. All t-derivatives vanish near the endpoints. Consequently g=dt^2+h_t matches under the mapping-torus gluing, including all normal derivatives, and is a smooth global metric.

Harmonic velocity one-form: for this metric, g(X,.)=alpha, |X|=1, and vol_g=mu. Since mu is independent of t, div_g X=0, equivalently delta_g alpha=0. Also d alpha=0. Thus Delta_H alpha=(d delta+delta d)alpha=0.

Stationary equation: the identity (nabla_X X)^flat=i_X d alpha+(1/2)d|X|^2 gives nabla_X X=0. Therefore with constant pressure p, the unforced steady incompressible Navier-Stokes equation with viscosity nu*Delta_H on the velocity one-form holds for every nu>0; every term vanishes. The sign convention for the Laplacian is immaterial here because its value is zero.

Actual computation and effective lift: retain the actual computable encoded input q_c and halting target H from the step-by-step disk construction. Work in a fixed product chart away from the seam: choose p_c=[q_c,1/2] and target W=image(H x (3/4,7/8)). During the nth traversal the base coordinate is phi^n(q_c); the positive trajectory meets W exactly when an iterate lies in H. Uniform input construction and target coding are inherited from that actual simulator, rather than manufactured by allowing arbitrary input-dependent open sets. The n=0 case is harmless because the chosen initial machine state is distinct from its halting state.
Energy and bounds: E=(1/2) integral_M |X|^2 vol_g=(1/2)Vol_g(M)<infinity. This metric is freely adapted to the simulator, exactly as allowed by Open problem 4.
counterevidence_and_limits: This supplies an answer only for the printed Hodge-Laplacian model and existence on some compact Riemannian three-manifold. It does not answer the fixed round-S3 or flat-T3 question in Open problem 3.

It does not prove robustness under arbitrary perturbations. Viscosity acts trivially here because the constructed one-form is harmonic; that is not the generic perturbation notion discussed in the cited compact robustness obstruction.
It does not extend automatically to a rough-Laplacian or strain-tensor viscosity model with different curvature terms. No assertion about those alternative equations is made.

It uses the earlier article's actual strong simulator, not only the abstract Definition 2.2 that the parent separately critiques. Proposition 4.1 itself remains an imported existence theorem; no new proof of that theorem is claimed.
This changes the stated open-problem scope, not the correctness of the main imported Euler constructions or the separate critical-metric proposition.
checks.repair: Narrow Open problem 4 to a specified metric or a different precise viscosity model, or acknowledge the affirmative suspension example for the Hodge model. Parent grading: bounded Minor scope/open-problem correction.

analytic_checks.claim: Under the surrounding finite-precision/ordinary computable-open reading, Definition2.2 permits halting information to be encoded in the target of an identity map.
proof: Fix the universal machine TU and number steps from1. For input c let r_c=2^(-t) if TU(c) first halts at step t, and0 if it never halts.

Uniform computability is explicit: for requested absolute error2^(-N), simulate N steps. Return2^(-t) if halting is observed, otherwise return0. If halting occurs later the error is at most2^(-(N+1)), and if never it is0. This is an approximation algorithm, not a halting decision.

In the unit disk D take the identity map and the fixed rational point p_c=(0,0). Let U_c=(-r_c,1/4) times (-1/4,1/4). Since0<=r_c<=1/2, it is a nonempty open rectangle contained in D; its endpoints are uniformly computable and it is uniformly effectively open. Its interval endpoint approximation is computable to arbitrary precision.

The positive orbit consists only of p_c. It meets U_c exactly when r_c>0, exactly when TU(c) halts. Thus this representation of computable open targets satisfies the printed definition while the dynamics do nothing.

An oracle deciding intersections of arbitrary computable sets applied to {p_c} and U_c decides ordinary halting. Remark4.4 cannot assume that this oracle preserves the undecidability of the original machine. Relativized halting for the stronger oracle is a different problem; the article has not supplied a simulation of all machines relative to that oracle.
analytic_checks.counterevidence_and_limits: This does not refute the actual reversible step-by-step encoding constructed in Sections4-5 or the cited Euler existence theorems. If a stronger finite geometric representation of target sets was intended, it must be specified and shown compatible with those constructions. A fixed target alone is not in general enough if arbitrary effective-open encodings remain allowed.
analytic_checks.repair: Specify uniformly effective simulation and restricted decoding/target representation, or impose the actual injective configuration-by-configuration simulation as part of the intended definition. Remove the unrestricted set-intersection oracle argument.

analytic_checks.claim: The local Bernoulli formula omits the squared speed.
proof: Metric compatibility and alpha=X^flat give (nabla_X X)^flat=i_X d alpha+(1/2)d|X|^2. Hence stationary Euler is i_X d alpha=-d(p+|X|^2/2).

The actual PDF writes p+||X||/2. The exact symbolic example X=(-y,x,0),p=(x^2+y^2)/2 is divergence-free and stationary. At(1,0,0), i_Xdalpha=(-2,0,0), whereas the negative derivative of the printed Bernoulli expression is(-3/2,0,0). The squared expression agrees identically.
analytic_checks.counterevidence_and_limits: A local missing exponent; it does not defeat the Reeb/Beltrami construction after correction.

analytic_checks.claim: The Reeb route yields stationary Euler fields for adapted metrics, within the stated non-prescribed metric setting.
proof: Cartan's formula gives L_R alpha=d(alpha(R))+i_R d alpha=0 and hence preservation of alpha wedge d alpha.

For h>0, i_(hR)((alpha wedge d alpha)/h)=d alpha, so the rescaled volume is invariant. A metric can be chosen with g(hR,.)=alpha and this volume by adjusting the positive metric on ker alpha; then curl(hR)=hR and pressure=-alpha(hR)/2 makes stationary Euler.

Conversely if curlX=fX with f nowherezero and X nonsingular, beta=X^flat satisfies beta wedge d beta=f|X|^2 mu, so beta is a contact form with the appropriate contact orientation and its Reeb field is X/|X|^2. This is the local algebra underlying the cited correspondence.

Positive time reparametrization preserves oriented orbits, so reachability transfers. For compact smooth nonsingular flows completeness is automatic; no Euclidean fixed-metric conclusion follows from choosing an adapted metric.
analytic_checks.limits: This verifies the displayed identities and conditional route; the full external global realization theorem and its effective construction are imported, not independently retrieved.

analytic_checks.claim: The new critical-metric conclusion admits a section-independent repair for the actual simulated construction.
proof: The actual formula for the standard section is omega=2*pi*k/l; it is correct. A different transverse disk need not have the same rotation number. For R_(2,1), section phi1=0 has return rotation pi, while section phi2=0 has identity return.

The identity collar of the constructed disk return map suspends to an open set of periodic flow orbits. An irrational weighted Hopf flow has only its two special closed circles, so cannot have that open set. Orbital conjugacy therefore forces l/k rational and all flow orbits closed.

A reversible universal machine has an initial nonhalting run with no repeated finite configuration. Otherwise simulating until halting or repetition would decide halting on every input. The injective step-by-step Cantor simulation yields an aperiodic return orbit, incompatible with all flow orbits closed.

Thus, conditional on the quoted critical-compatible-to-Sasakian and Sasakian-to-weighted-Hopf classifications, the selected universal construction cannot admit the stated compatible critical metric. This repair does not use the insufficient weak reachability definition or the oracle claim.
analytic_checks.limits: External classifications [18] and[2] were not materialized in the bounded source manifest and were not independently read. The conclusion is restricted to the chosen universal construction, not every Reeb field realizing an arbitrary disk map in Theorem4.1.

analytic_checks.claim: The Hodge-viscosity formulation of OpenProblem4 admits an adapted-metric suspension construction.
analytic_checks.attribution: Native later helper proposed the suspension argument; primary executor independently checked its gluing, volume, differential identities and simulation transfer. No second runtime experiment is claimed.
proof: Use the article's area-preserving disk diffeomorphism phi, identity on a boundary collar, with its actual step-by-step universal simulation. Extend it by identity to a closed oriented surface Sigma=S^2 with area form omega agreeing on the disk.
Form M=(Sigma times[0,1])/((x,1)~(phi(x),0)). X=partial_t,alpha=dt and mu=dt wedge omega descend since phi preserves omega. M is smooth closed compact.

Choose h0 with area form omega. Let k_t=(1-beta(t))h0+beta(t)phi^*h0, where beta=0 near0 and1 near1, and write vol(k_t)=f_t omega. In dimension2, h_t=k_t/f_t has area omega. Endpoints are h0 andphi^*h0, with all time derivatives zero near the endpoints, so g=dt^2+h_t glues smoothly.

With this metric X^flat=dt,|X|=1,vol_g=mu and divX=0. Thus d alpha=0,delta alpha=0 and Delta_H alpha=0. The covariant identity gives nabla_X X=0. Constant pressure and X solve unforced steady Navier-Stokes for every viscosity, regardless of the sign convention for the vanishing Hodge term.

The section t=1/2 has return map phi. Input points and halting targets lift in that product chart with a target time strip inside(1/2,1), so actual discrete simulation and its reachability reduction persist. Energy is Vol_g(M)/2, finite by compactness.
analytic_checks.limits: The metric and manifold are freely chosen, exactly as in OpenProblem4, and viscosity is specifically the Hodge Laplacian of Remark6.1. This gives no fixed round/flat metric solution, no perturbation robustness and no conclusion for different viscous operators. The imported existence of the simulated area-preserving map remains an explicit premise.
